passages.text: Business Execution and Supply Chain Risks Risk: Competition from illicit trade Description: Illicit trade in the form of counterfeit products, diversion of genuine Group products, products that are smuggled illegally across borders, and locally manufactured products, which do not comply with applicable regulations and/or in which applicable taxes are evaded, has had a significant impact and continues to represent a significant and growing threat to the legitimate tobacco industry, including New Categories products. Factors such as increasing levels of taxation and inflation, economic downturn and increased cost of living, lack of law enforcement, appropriate penalties and weak border control are encouraging more adult tobacco and New Categories consumers to switch to illegal cheaper tobacco and New Categories products and are providing greater rewards for counterfeiters and smugglers. Regulatory restrictions such as plain packaging or graphic health warnings, display bans, flavour or ingredient restrictions and increased compliance costs further disadvantage legitimate industry participants by providing competitive advantages to illicit manufacturers and distributors of illicit tobacco and New Categories products. Impact: Illicit trade has an overall negative impact on society, deprives governments of revenues and encourages various forms of crime such as terrorism, money laundering and human trafficking. Above all, illicit trade has an adverse effect on the Group’s overall business and reputation. Illicit trade can damage brand equity, which could undermine the Group’s investment in Trade Marketing and Distribution, increase operational costs where products may become commoditised, make it more difficult to adhere to underage prevention and decrease volumes sold. Although anti-illicit trade is an integral part of our Standards of Business Conduct (SoBC), representing our internal commitment in the fight against illicit trade and setting out the controls all Group companies must have in place and adhere to, it cannot prevent all instances of illicit trade. Furthermore, counterfeit products (especially New Categories) and other illicit products could harm consumers, damages goodwill and/or the category (with lower volumes and reduced profits), and could potentially lead to misplaced claims against BAT, further regulation and a failure to deliver our corporate harm reduction objective. Illicit trade may also reduce the Group’s ability to take price increases due to competitive pressure from cheaper illegal products. Finally, as the Group has contractual and legislative obligations to prevent the diversion of our products into illicit channels, actual breaches of the obligations to prevent product diversion into illicit channels have resulted, and may continue to result, in substantial fines in the forms of seizure payments and legislative penalties (including financial penalties ). Additionally, actual and perceived breaches may result in the risk of reputational damage (including negative perceptions of our governance and our sustainability credentials) from Group products being found in illicit channels. credit_strengths.text: Operating margin materially exceeds the Consumer Staples sector median, reflecting premium pricing power and a high-margin combustible portfolio that funds New Categories investment. This structural profitability supports internal cash generation even as revenue declines modestly year over year, providing a durable buffer for fixed charges and shareholder returns.

Free cash flow comfortably covers capital expenditure, with capex representing a modest share of operating cash flow. This leaves substantial discretionary cash for debt reduction and distributions, a key credit strength given the issuer's significant absolute debt burden and the sector's generally stable cash conversion profile.

key_risks.text: Illicit trade in counterfeit and smuggled tobacco and New Categories products represents a concrete disclosed risk, eroding volumes, brand equity and pricing power while exposing the Group to seizure payments and legislative penalties. This threat is intensifying with higher taxation and weak enforcement, directly pressuring revenue and margins in both developed and emerging markets.

The debt stack is substantial and refinancing-sensitive, with borrowings concentrated in long-term instruments and no disclosed maturity ladder in the bundle. Absent a detailed maturity profile, we cannot assess near-term refinancing concentration, which is material given the absolute debt size and the issuer's ongoing buyback programme.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage sits below the sector median, indicating that operating income covers interest expense less comfortably than peers. While the absolute coverage level remains adequate, the gap to sector median suggests limited headroom if operating income deteriorates or refinancing costs rise, warranting close monitoring of fixed-charge coverage trends.

Free cash flow to debt is below the sector median, reflecting the heavy absolute debt load relative to cash generation. Although free cash flow is substantial, its conversion to debt reduction is constrained by shareholder distributions, including buybacks, which absorb a meaningful portion of discretionary cash and slow deleveraging.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is Significant, driven by a cash-flow tier at the lower bound and missing EBITDA-based leverage metrics. Revenue has declined over the past three years while debt has reduced, but the absence of depreciation and amortization data prevents a full leverage assessment, a material gap for evaluating the capital structure.

Our forward view is that credit quality remains supported by high margins and robust free cash flow, but deleveraging will be gradual given buybacks and dividends. The current ratio below one and a Grey Altman Z-score signal some balance-sheet caution. We would need a full maturity profile and EBITDA data to refine the risk assessment.

credit_strengths.text: 營運利潤率大幅高於消費必需品行業中位數，反映其高端定價能力及高利潤率的可燃產品組合，為新類別投資提供資金。此結構性盈利能力支持內部現金生成，即使收入按年溫和下降，仍為固定費用及股東回報提供持久緩衝。
自由現金流從容覆蓋資本開支，資本開支僅佔營運現金流的一小部分。這為減債及分派留下大量可自由支配現金，鑑於發行人的絕對債務負擔龐大及行業現金轉換狀況普遍穩定，此為關鍵信用優勢。

key_risks.text: 假冒及走私煙草及新類別產品的非法貿易為一項具體披露的風險，侵蝕銷量、品牌權益及定價能力，同時使集團面臨沒收付款及立法罰款。隨著稅負加重及執法薄弱，此威脅正在加劇，直接對已發展及新興市場的收入及利潤率構成壓力。
債務結構龐大且對再融資敏感，借款集中於長期工具，且文件中未披露到期日階梯。缺乏詳細到期情況，我們無法評估近期再融資集中度，鑑於絕對債務規模及發行人持續進行的回購計劃，此點屬重大。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率低於行業中位數，顯示營運收入覆蓋利息支出的舒適度低於同業。雖然絕對覆蓋水平仍屬足夠，但與行業中位數的差距意味著若營運收入惡化或再融資成本上升，緩衝空間有限，需密切監察固定費用覆蓋趨勢。
自由現金流對債務比率低於行業中位數，反映相對於現金生成，絕對債務負擔沉重。儘管自由現金流可觀，但其轉化為減債受到股東分派（包括回購）的限制，該等分派吸收相當部分可自由支配現金並拖慢去槓桿化。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險狀況為顯著，受現金流層級處於下限及缺乏基於EBITDA的槓桿指標所驅動。過去三年收入下降而債務減少，但缺乏折舊及攤銷數據阻礙全面槓桿評估，此為評估資本結構的重大缺口。
我們的前瞻觀點是信用質量仍受高利潤率及強勁自由現金流支持，但鑑於回購及股息，去槓桿化將屬漸進。流動比率低於一及Altman Z-score為灰色地帶，顯示資產負債表存在一定審慎。我們需要完整的到期情況及EBITDA數據以完善風險評估。
